target.title: feat: add Orgo provider
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a delegated-run Orgo provider for Linux cloud computers.

- Registers `provider: orgo` with alias `orgo-ai`.
- Creates an owned workspace/computer, waits for readiness, runs Bash commands through the API, and performs guarded cleanup.
- Keeps Orgo outside SSH/rsync and coordinator flows; runs require `--no-sync`.
- Adds provider configuration, docs, generated metadata, lifecycle coverage, and a guarded live harness.

## Maintainer triage

Current head: `2fd67f9d0b276a9b59002345034a639d4e3aab84`.

A current-`main` repair candidate was exercised locally with ownership scoping, durable create/delete state, strict API envelopes, exact identity checks, legacy-claim migration, bounded cleanup proof, full race tests, and structured AutoReview. It was intentionally not pushed because the final review exposed a provider-contract safety blocker that cannot be repaired with another local inference layer.

Orgo's workspace delete endpoint is unconditionally cascading: it deletes the workspace **and every computer in it**. The API documents no ETag, version, conditional-delete precondition, or non-cascading mode. Therefore `GET workspace (empty)` followed by `DELETE workspace` has an unavoidable race: another client can add a computer between those requests and Crabbox would delete that unrelated computer.

Relevant provider contracts:

- https://docs.orgo.ai/api-reference/workspaces/delete
- https://docs.orgo.ai/api-reference/workspaces/get
- https://docs.orgo.ai/api-reference/workspaces/list
- https://docs.orgo.ai/api-reference/introduction

## Decision required

Do not merge yet. Choose one product/API direction:

1. Defer until Orgo provides a conditional/versioned workspace delete or a non-cascading delete primitive.
2. Redesign the provider to require an operator-managed workspace and manage only exact claimed computers; Crabbox would never delete workspaces.
3. Close the built-in provider proposal and keep Orgo as an external/custom integration.

The operator-managed-workspace option is the smallest safe feature, but it is a user-visible contract change and needs maintainer acceptance before implementation.

## Verification state

- Historical exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/28797692625 — 7/7 passed, but it predates current `main` and does not prove the repair candidate.
- The live pull-request branch is conflicting and substantially behind current `main`; all local and hosted gates must be rerun after a product direction is chosen.
- No funded Orgo credential is available for the required hosted create -> ready -> Bash marker -> computer delete -> zero-resource lifecycle. Orgo currently advertises a paid minimum plan, so this remains a separate explicit-spend gate.
